text:
It is truly heartwarming to witness the modern obsession with wax, that miraculous, flammable sludge harvested from the corpses of dead animals or the refined tears of ancient trees. We have elevated this simple, sticky byproduct to the status of a spiritual beacon, lighting it up to create a "cozy ambiance" while ignoring the fact that we are essentially playing with fire in a tube of solidified fat.

The primary material of a candle is, of course, wax. But let’s be honest, it’s not just wax; it’s a metaphor for our collective inability to handle darkness without a $40 artisanal scent profile. Whether it’s soy, beeswax, or paraffin, the point is that we pay a premium to watch a solid object slowly melt into a puddle of its own destruction, all while pretending it’s self-care. It’s the only time we celebrate something literally burning itself out, calling it "relaxation" instead of "slow combustion hazard." Truly, if we applied this same logic to our actual problems, we’d just light a "Vanilla Bean" candle and hope the universe provides a soundtrack.
